difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that each of the separation axioms of the chapter is stable under composition of morphisms of formal algebraic spaces (statement lines 6862-6867). The proof factors the diagonal of the composite through the two obvious maps, observing that the diagonal of the composite over the base of the second morphism is the composite of the diagonal of the second morphism with the map from the fibre product over the middle object to the fibre product over the base (proof lines 6869-6876). Since each axiom is defined by requiring the diagonal to have some property, the proof invokes the earlier statement identifying the property of the second arrow in that factorisation, and concludes because the property in question is stable under composition of representable morphisms (proof lines 6874-6882). The claim is H2: the argument identifies the factorisation of the diagonal, transfers the property to the second factor by a named result, and applies stability under composition, so it is short but complete.
